memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Chronic urticaria.
Patient reports daily wheals and itching for 8 months, worse in evenings, mild facial swelling. Examination shows scattered erythematous wheals on trunk and limbs, no angioedema. Vital signs normal. No smoking history. CBC and thyroid function tests ordered.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Levocetirizine 5 mg tablet, take orally once daily in the morning. Continue for 3 months, review.

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
CBC: WBC 6.2 x10^9/L, neutrophils 4.1, lymphocytes 1.8, eosinophils 0.3 x10^9/L (reference 0.0-0.5). Hemoglobin 12.8 g/dL, platelets 240 x10^9/L.
Thyroid function: TSH 2.1 mIU/L (0.4-4.0), free T4 13.2 pmol/L (10-22).

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I have been taking the levocetirizine each morning. The hives are less intense now, only a few spots appear after long drives. Itching at night has decreased but I still wake up scratching occasionally.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Chronic urticaria, partially controlled.
Patient notes improvement in daytime wheals but reports nocturnal itching and occasional breakthrough wheals after stress. Examination: faint scattered wheals on arms, no dermal thickening. No smoking. Continue antihistamine, add nighttime cetirizine.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Levocetirizine 5 mg tablet, take orally once daily in the morning.
Cetirizine 10 mg tablet, take orally at bedtime. Review in 8 weeks.

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
CBC: WBC 5.9 x10^9/L, neutrophils 3.9, lymphocytes 1.7, eosinophils 0.2 x10^9/L (ref 0.0-0.5). Hemoglobin 13.0 g/dL, platelets 235 x10^9/L.
Thyroid function: TSH 1.9 mIU/L (0.4-4.0), free T4 13.5 pmol/L (10-22).

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Follow‑up appointment booked for 2025-09-05 at 10:30 AM with Dr Suresh Menon (D05) in Pulmonology clinic. Please arrive 10 minutes early.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Chronic urticaria, well controlled.
Patient reports only occasional mild wheals after heavy exertion, no nocturnal itching. Examination: skin clear, no wheals. No smoking. Continue current regimen, consider tapering cetirizine if symptom‑free for another month.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Levocetirizine 5 mg tablet, take orally once daily in the morning.
Cetirizine 10 mg tablet, take orally at bedtime – to be stopped if symptom‑free for 4 weeks.

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
CBC: WBC 6.0 x10^9/L, neutrophils 4.0, lymphocytes 1.8, eosinophils 0.2 x10^9/L (ref 0.0-0.5). Hemoglobin 12.9 g/dL, platelets 238 x10^9/L.
Thyroid function: TSH 2.0 mIU/L (0.4-4.0), free T4 13.3 pmol/L (10-22).

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Over the past two weeks the hives have returned, especially after early morning shifts. I get itchy patches on my neck and forearms that last a few hours. I stopped the cetirizine a month ago as advised, but levocetirizine alone does not seem enough now.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Chronic urticaria, flare.
Patient describes recurrent wheals on neck and forearms linked to early‑morning work, mild nocturnal itching. Examination: scattered erythematous wheals on upper trunk and arms, no angioedema. No smoking. Restart nighttime cetirizine and review levocetirizine dose.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Levocetirizine 5 mg tablet, take orally once daily in the morning.
Cetirizine 10 mg tablet, take orally at bedtime. Continue for 6 weeks, then reassess.

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
CBC: WBC 6.3 x10^9/L, neutrophils 4.2, lymphocytes 1.9, eosinophils 0.3 x10^9/L (ref 0.0-0.5). Hemoglobin 13.1 g/dL, platelets 242 x10^9/L.
Thyroid function: TSH 2.2 mIU/L (0.4-4.0), free T4 13.0 pmol/L (10-22).

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Chronic urticaria, controlled.
Patient reports only occasional mild wheals after intense physical activity, no nocturnal symptoms. Examination: skin clear, no wheals. No smoking, pack‑years 0. Advise to maintain levocetirizine OD and keep cetirizine PRN for breakthrough symptoms.
